Abstract  
This research aimed to: 1) develop a car rental management system, and 2) study user satisfaction with the car rental management system. The system development process followed the SDLC cycle. The research sample consisted of 30 representatives selected through purposive sampling. The instrument used was a satisfaction evaluation form for the car rental management system. The system was developed using the PHP framework, with W3Schools as a learning website for code, which is similar to the popular Bootstrap. CSS and JavaScript were also used in the system’s development, and Apache 8.6.0 was utilized as the web server. The car rental management system itself was used as a tool for collecting satisfaction evaluation data. Statistics used in the research included mean and standard deviation. The research findings are as follows: 1) The car rental management system consists of three parts: the general user section (view only), the member section (can reserve cars and make payments under specified conditions), and the administrator section (can manage basic information, approve reservations, and verify payments). 2) User satisfaction with the system was found to be at a high level, with an average score of 4.27. The system allows users to benefit from online car rentals without traveling to the shop, and also increases business revenue channels.

Keywords: system development, management system, car rental, MVC web application  
Science and Technology to Community Journal, Vol. 1, No. 4, July – August 2023 1 No. 1 No. Introduction

The car rental business has become increasingly popular and attractive among today’s entrepreneurs due to its flexibility and ease of operation. Simply owning one’s own vehicle enables an individual to rent it out to those in need of transportation. Most car rental business owners started with renting out just a few vehicles and gradually expanded into larger-scale car rental businesses, offering a wider variety of vehicles. In fact, according to business analysis statistics, every province in Thailand now has at least one car rental provider. As of June 30, 2022, there were a total of 2,045 active businesses in the car and motorcycle rental sector across Thailand (Department of Business Development, 2022). A car rental business is similar to renting out a house or condominium, but in this business, income is generated by leasing vehicles. The vehicle owner or lessor rents out their own car to individuals who need a vehicle for driving in accordance with their intended purpose. Types of vehicles available for rent include private cars, motorcycles, vans, trucks, and other types of vehicles. Renters are required to pay the rental fee as stipulated in the vehicle rental agreement made jointly with the owner.

There are two types of car rental: 
1) Operating leases, which involve long-term rentals based on a contract. The renter pays monthly rental fees and is responsible for fuel costs, while the lessor is responsible for maintenance, insurance, and other related expenses. This type of lease is suitable for large-scale operators with a diverse vehicle fleet, and the primary clients are usually private companies, government agencies, or state enterprises.
2) Short-term rentals, where cars are rented out only for a short period—daily, weekly, or monthly. These may include private cars, vans, pickups, or motorcycles. This type of lease suits small-scale operators who wish to rent out their personal vehicles, with customers mainly being general individuals or tourists. Currently, as many groups of tourists visit Thailand and face travel challenges within the area, this type of service has grown popular (Ngern Tid Lor, 2023).

The traditional service system in car rental shops involved the following process: when a customer wished to rent a car, the renter was required to present an ID card and a driver’s license to the shop as proof for vehicle rental. After the renter selected a car, the staff would fill out a car rental form and record the return date, storing this information in a file folder. The staff handled payment collection for the rental, and upon return, would check the return date and inspect the vehicle for any damages in order to calculate fines or repair costs if necessary. When new vehicles arrived, the shop purchased cars and made them available for rental in the “new vehicles” section. Clearly, the traditional system relied on manual labor at every step, which led to delays in providing rental service. For instance, issues like recording the return date or handing over the vehicle could be delayed, as a single staff member may oversee multiple rentals, causing confusion. This might result in issues such as incorrect recording of return dates, or failing to remember if a specific customer had previously borrowed a car before renting again. 1 No. July 4, 2023 – August 2023  
Once again, receipts were not provided to customers, as the store had not collected customer data or information about the vehicles in the shop (Chatchai Khorta, 2013; Kanda Sirichanprawech, 2021). With an understanding of the aforementioned issues, the development process for the system was studied. Therefore, in order to address these problems, the researcher recognized the existing challenges and identified a solution: the creation of a car rental management system. This system aims to make the processes of car rental and return more efficient, as well as assist in managing the necessary database for the business, preventing data loss and reducing redundancy. SQL Server is used for database management. The system is developed using the PHP framework, with W3Schools serving as a website for code learning, similar to the widely used Bootstrap. CSS and JavaScript are also utilized in development. Apache 8.6.0 functions as the web server program. 

Research methodology: Population and sample groups
1. Population: The general public who have used car rental services or possess relevant knowledge
2. The sample group consisted of 30 members of the general public, selected using purposive sampling. Prior to completing the evaluation form, participants were shown a sample video about car rental or provided with background knowledge on car rental. The research instruments for developing the car rental management system included a system usability satisfaction assessment form and the car rental management system itself. Relevant theoretical background: 1) MVC (Model-View-Controller). MVC applies Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) principles by dividing main functions into objects, specifically model, view, and controller, with strict separation of responsibilities. – Model: The model component is responsible for all data operations, preparing suitable data and operating only upon a request from the controller. – View: The view handles all interface aspects or user interfaces, receiving instructions from the controller and acting as an intermediary between the user and the controller. – Controller: The controller functions as the brain and central processing unit of the system; it interacts with all components, coordinating all logic in the system. 2) OOP (Object-Oriented Programming) is a method of programming based on the concept of objects. It provides data encapsulation and inheritance, which has led to OOP being widely accepted and adopted in the development of various systems, such as the Windows operating system. The history of the OOP concept stems from the traditional approach to programming, which was to solve problems using computers as tools, much like using calculators for mathematical problems. The new approach to programming emphasizes the problem and its components (in order to solve it). This emphasis on the problem and its components (the problem space) is similar to solving issues and the necessities of human life, which involve people, animals, and things tasked with problem-solving, rather than focusing on the ways or steps to solve the problem (the solution space), which is the old style of programming. Alan Kay proposed five rules as the foundation of object-oriented programming (OOP) languages as follows:  
- Everything is an object.  
- A program is a bunch of objects telling each other what to do by sending messages.  
- Each object has its own memory made up of other objects.  
- Every object has a type.  
- Objects of the same type receive the same kinds of messages. (Anon Longhan, 2013)  

Steps of the research process  
The development process for the car rental management system followed the system development life cycle (SDLC) (Kitivath Kittivatana, 2016), consisting of seven steps as follows:  
1) Problem recognition: In car rental management, operational processes are complicated. Managing a car rental business may require a large number of staff for supervision.  
2) Feasibility study: The results indicate that currently, the application of computer technology to the development of car rental management systems helps make management significantly more convenient and attracts an increasing number of service users.  
3) Analysis: System analysis uses data flow diagrams (DFDs) to clearly visualize the system’s workflow. The DFD starts by giving an overview of the system before breaking down the operations into subcomponents. 4) Design: The system database was designed by determining data management categories, such as car information management, car rental reservation management, bank information management, and member system, among others. This design considered data storage capability, accuracy, ease of use, and data security.  
5) Construction: The tools used included a satisfaction assessment form for the use of the car rental management system. The software development followed a structured MVC format. The database was designed and developed using MySQL database management software. The website was then built using Dreamweaver, with PHP programming used to control data storage in the database management system. The PHP framework, with W3Schools serving as a website for code learning, was used. The system operated under the Windows operating system and was accessed via a web browser. The website consisted of functions for data insertion, deletion, searching, updating, editing, and data display.  
6) Conversion: After developing the car rental management system on a simulated server (localhost), the database system was installed on the web server for system testing and to assess user satisfaction. Feedback was collected for further improvements.  
7) Maintenance: A user manual for the car rental management system was created, providing guidance for both the system administrator and members. Evaluation forms were designed to assess user satisfaction with the car rental management system. Statistical methods used in the research included mean and standard deviation, with results assessed according to a 5-level evaluation scale: highest, high, moderate, low, and lowest. The evaluation (Boonchom Srisawat, 2010) can be interpreted as follows: a mean score between 4.50 - 5.00 indicates the highest level, 3.50 – 4.49 indicates a high level, 2.50 - 3.49 indicates a moderate level, 1.50 – 2.49 indicates a low level, and 1.00 – 1.49 indicates the lowest level.

Research Results  
The researcher divided the presentation of research findings into two parts according to the objectives:  
1) To develop a car rental management system  
2) To assess the usability quality of the car rental management system  
The details are as follows:

1) Results of the Development of the Car Rental Management System  
The car rental management system has three types of users: administrators, members, and general users. It enables management of various types of information as follows:  
1.1) General users (non-members) can access car information details and may register as members to use the car rental reservation system. Users are required to have a certain level of technological proficiency.

In cases where cars are returned later than the customer’s specified time, the business still enforces fines by cash or direct bank transfer in front of the car rental provider using the following conditions: vehicles with 1,200 cc engines incur a late fee of 214 baht/hour, 1,500 cc vehicles incur 268 baht/hour, and vehicles with 1,600–1,800 cc engines incur 321 baht/hour (Ecocar, 2020). From Table 1, the results of the usability satisfaction assessment of the car rental management system by 30 Computer Science students, based on a five-point Likert scale across two aspects and eight items, reveal an overall mean satisfaction score of 4.27, which is considered high. When examining individual items, the performance aspect—specifically item 1, "the system accurately manages vehicle data," and item 3, "the system responds quickly"—received the highest average scores at 4.39. Discussion of Results  
The rapid data exchange over the internet has facilitated the development of a self-service reservation system, reducing errors inherent in traditional booking methods and enabling independent booking management. Additionally, the developed system allows for fast and highly accurate information retrieval, as well as storage and editing of various essential data such as car reservation information, rental data, vehicle information, and payment details, with easy data searchability. These results are consistent with previous research, such as that by Usanee Mueansaweang (2017), who developed an online daily/monthly car booking and rental system for Aunsang Dormitory. Their findings indicated that the system could store diverse data and provided rapid searching and retrieval capabilities. Furthermore, the developed system could accurately calculate reservation fees and automatically generate reservation confirmations and receipts, along with offering online payment notifications, reducing errors and increasing the accuracy and reliability of calculations, thus building user trust.  
This also aligns with the MVC concept (BorntoDev, 2022), which divides main functionalities into objects named Model, View, and Controller; the operations of these three objects are clearly separated. This principle was also applied by the system developers to address the aforementioned challenges.  
Additionally, these findings correspond with Wachirawit Nilsuk et al. (2021), who designed and developed a personal car rental system on the internet using a structural approach, comprising three modules: car owner, administrator, and renter. The system usability evaluation indicated a high quality level. Moreover, Veerapon Panurak et al. (2020) developed a tourism promotion innovation—an automatic bicycle rental system using QR code technology—consisting of nine subsystems: member registration, membership management, bicycle rental, rental management, bicycle management, payment, bicycle return, notification, and reporting. Community satisfaction surveys on the tourism promotion innovation found that overall satisfaction across all items was at the highest level.  
Conclusion and Suggestions  
It can be concluded that the car rental management system serves three types of users: administrators, members, and general users. The system can manage the following information:  
1) General users can view car rental reservation details and register as members to access online car rental reservation services.  
2) Members can reserve cars online, select car size and seating, calculate prices and confirm online reservations, notify payment per the reservation slip, print online reservation slips, view reservation data via situation reports, search reservation details, edit their personal data, change passwords, log out, check details of cars available for rent, and ask questions via the web board.  
3) Administrators

The system is able to manage, add, edit, delete, and search for online reservation data, bank information, and payment notification details. It allows for the specification of reservation dates, manages member information, reservation order records, booking reports, rental car information, as well as monitoring and responding to questions on the web board. User satisfaction with the car rental management system, as reported by 30 users, was rated at a high level, with a mean score of 4.27, indicating that the system is indeed functional and usable.  
Suggestions: This research was developed under the Windows operating system and accessed via a web browser. If further developed as a mobile application, it would broaden the user base. Additionally, the system’s design and interface currently lack visual appeal, and it should be improved to be more attractive and modern.

Abstract  
This research aimed to: 1) develop a car rental management system, and 2) study user satisfaction with the car rental management system. The system development process followed the SDLC cycle. The research sample consisted of 30 representatives selected through purposive sampling. The instrument used was a satisfaction evaluation form for the car rental management system. The system was developed using the PHP framework, with W3Schools as a learning website for code, which is similar to the popular Bootstrap. CSS and JavaScript were also used in the system’s development, and Apache 8.6.0 was utilized as the web server. The car rental management system itself was used as a tool for collecting satisfaction evaluation data. Statistics used in the research included mean and standard deviation. The research findings are as follows: 1) The car rental management system consists of three parts: the general user section (view only), the member section (can reserve cars and make payments under specified conditions), and the administrator section (can manage basic information, approve reservations, and verify payments). 2) User satisfaction with the system was found to be at a high level, with an average score of 4.27. The system allows users to benefit from online car rentals without traveling to the shop, and also increases business revenue channels.

Introduction

The car rental business has become increasingly popular and attractive among today’s entrepreneurs due to its flexibility and ease of operation. Simply owning one’s own vehicle enables an individual to rent it out to those in need of transportation. Most car rental business owners started with renting out just a few vehicles and gradually expanded into larger-scale car rental businesses, offering a wider variety of vehicles. In fact, according to business analysis statistics, every province in Thailand now has at least one car rental provider. As of June 30, 2022, there were a total of 2,045 active businesses in the car and motorcycle rental sector across Thailand (Department of Business Development, 2022). A car rental business is similar to renting out a house or condominium, but in this business, income is generated by leasing vehicles. The vehicle owner or lessor rents out their own car to individuals who need a vehicle for driving in accordance with their intended purpose. Types of vehicles available for rent include private cars, motorcycles, vans, trucks, and other types of vehicles. Renters are required to pay the rental fee as stipulated in the vehicle rental agreement made jointly with the owner.

There are two types of car rental: 
1) Operating leases, which involve long-term rentals based on a contract. The renter pays monthly rental fees and is responsible for fuel costs, while the lessor is responsible for maintenance, insurance, and other related expenses. This type of lease is suitable for large-scale operators with a diverse vehicle fleet, and the primary clients are usually private companies, government agencies, or state enterprises.
2) Short-term rentals, where cars are rented out only for a short period—daily, weekly, or monthly. These may include private cars, vans, pickups, or motorcycles. This type of lease suits small-scale operators who wish to rent out their personal vehicles, with customers mainly being general individuals or tourists. Currently, as many groups of tourists visit Thailand and face travel challenges within the area, this type of service has grown popular (Ngern Tid Lor, 2023).

The traditional service system in car rental shops involved the following process: when a customer wished to rent a car, the renter was required to present an ID card and a driver’s license to the shop as proof for vehicle rental. After the renter selected a car, the staff would fill out a car rental form and record the return date, storing this information in a file folder. The staff handled payment collection for the rental, and upon return, would check the return date and inspect the vehicle for any damages in order to calculate fines or repair costs if necessary. When new vehicles arrived, the shop purchased cars and made them available for rental in the “new vehicles” section. Clearly, the traditional system relied on manual labor at every step, which led to delays in providing rental service. For instance, issues like recording the return date or handing over the vehicle could be delayed, as a single staff member may oversee multiple rentals, causing confusion. This might result in issues such as incorrect recording of return dates, or failing to remember if a specific customer had previously borrowed a car before renting again.

2) OOP (Object-Oriented Programming) is a method of programming based on the concept of objects. It provides data encapsulation and inheritance, which has led to OOP being widely accepted and adopted in the development of various systems, such as the Windows operating system. The history of the OOP concept stems from the traditional approach to programming, which was to solve problems using computers as tools, much like using calculators for mathematical problems. The new approach to programming emphasizes the problem and its components (in order to solve it). This emphasis on the problem and its components (the problem space) is similar to solving issues and the necessities of human life, which involve people, animals, and things tasked with problem-solving, rather than focusing on the ways or steps to solve the problem (the solution space), which is the old style of programming. Alan Kay proposed five rules as the foundation of object-oriented programming (OOP) languages as follows:  
- Everything is an object.  
- A program is a bunch of objects telling each other what to do by sending messages.  
- Each object has its own memory made up of other objects.  
- Every object has a type.  
- Objects of the same type receive the same kinds of messages. (Anon Longhan, 2013)

This design considered data storage capability, accuracy, ease of use, and data security.  
5) Construction: The tools used included a satisfaction assessment form for the use of the car rental management system. The software development followed a structured MVC format. The PHP framework, with W3Schools serving as a website for code learning, was used. The system operated under the Windows operating system and was accessed via a web browser. The website consisted of functions for data insertion, deletion, searching, updating, editing, and data display.  
6) Conversion: After developing the car rental management system on a simulated server (localhost), the database system was installed on the web server for system testing and to assess user satisfaction. Feedback was collected for further improvements.  
7) Maintenance: A user manual for the car rental management system was created, providing guidance for both the system administrator and members. Evaluation forms were designed to assess user satisfaction with the car rental management system. Statistical methods used in the research included mean and standard deviation, with results assessed according to a 5-level evaluation scale: highest, high, moderate, low, and lowest. The evaluation (Boonchom Srisawat, 2010) can be interpreted as follows: a mean score between 4.50 - 5.00 indicates the highest level, 3.50 – 4.49 indicates a high level, 2.50 - 3.49 indicates a moderate level, 1.50 – 2.49 indicates a low level, and 1.00 – 1.49 indicates the lowest level.

Discussion of Results  
The rapid data exchange over the internet has facilitated the development of a self-service reservation system, reducing errors inherent in traditional booking methods and enabling independent booking management. Additionally, the developed system allows for fast and highly accurate information retrieval, as well as storage and editing of various essential data such as car reservation information, rental data, vehicle information, and payment details, with easy data searchability. These results are consistent with previous research, such as that by Usanee Mueansaweang (2017), who developed an online daily/monthly car booking and rental system for Aunsang Dormitory. Their findings indicated that the system could store diverse data and provided rapid searching and retrieval capabilities. Furthermore, the developed system could accurately calculate reservation fees and automatically generate reservation confirmations and receipts, along with offering online payment notifications, reducing errors and increasing the accuracy and reliability of calculations, thus building user trust.  
This also aligns with the MVC concept (BorntoDev, 2022), which divides main functionalities into objects named Model, View, and Controller; the operations of these three objects are clearly separated. This principle was also applied by the system developers to address the aforementioned challenges.  
Additionally, these findings correspond with Wachirawit Nilsuk et al. (2021), who designed and developed a personal car rental system on the internet using a structural approach, comprising three modules: car owner, administrator, and renter. The system usability evaluation indicated a high quality level. Moreover, Veerapon Panurak et al. (2020) developed a tourism promotion innovation—an automatic bicycle rental system using QR code technology—consisting of nine subsystems: member registration, membership management, bicycle rental, rental management, bicycle management, payment, bicycle return, notification, and reporting. Community satisfaction surveys on the tourism promotion innovation found that overall satisfaction across all items was at the highest level.  
Conclusion and Suggestions  
It can be concluded that the car rental management system serves three types of users: administrators, members, and general users. The system can manage the following information:  
1) General users can view car rental reservation details and register as members to access online car rental reservation services.  
2) Members can reserve cars online, select car size and seating, calculate prices and confirm online reservations, notify payment per the reservation slip, print online reservation slips, view reservation data via situation reports, search reservation details, edit their personal data, change passwords, log out, check details of cars available for rent, and ask questions via the web board.
